* Prepare presentations and recommendations for management.

**About Syenta**  
Syenta is pioneering a new era in semiconductor manufacturing with our groundbreaking Localized Electrochemical Manufacturing (LEM) technology. Our manufacturing products build cutting edge advanced packaging for the semiconductor industry by combining patterning and metallization into a single tool. We do that by achieving high-speed, high-resolution metallization at significantly lower costs and energy use, while minimizing emissions and waste.

Founded in Australia, our growing footprint in the US represents a key milestone in our journey. We are building a world-class team where seasoned engineers and ambitious emerging talent collaborate to solve some of the toughest challenges in semiconductor manufacturing.

**About the Role**

We are seeking a **Process Engineer** **Intern** to join Syenta’s Sydney process team **immediately**. This will be a **6-month full-time internship**. You’ll be working directly on the processes at the heart of Syenta’s technology - running experiments, developing your technical understanding, and contributing ideas that genuinely shape how we work.

From day one you’ll have real deliberate mentorship from senior experts who are invested in your development. We’re looking for someone who is hungry to learn, takes ownership of their work, and wants to make an impact at a company redefining how semiconductors are made.

**Responsibilities**

*Process & Experimentation*

* Following existing standard operating procedures (SOPs) to support Syenta’s stamp fabrication process and stamp pre-plating process through hands-on laboratory work, experimental runs, and active participation in team discussions.
* Execute parameter sweeps, design of experiments (DOE) runs, and repeatability tests, growing into increasing ownership of experimental design over time.
* Prepare substrates, consumables, and materials; operate prototype equipment with guidance; and perform routine maintenance and troubleshooting.

*Data & Analysis*

* Maintain clear and accurate records of all laboratory work to ensure reproducibility and knowledge sharing across the team.
* Assist with data analysis, plotting, and summary reporting.
* Identify anomalies and unexpected results and work collaboratively with the team to investigate and understand them.

*Communication & Collaboration*

* Work alongside the broader team to achieve technical milestones and resolve issues as they arise.
* Share progress updates with the LEM team and actively contribute to group discussions on results and next steps.
* Support preparation and delivery of demonstrations of Syenta’s LEM technology to visitors, partners, and investors.

*Ownership & Impact*

* Take ownership of assigned projects and deliverables, seeing them through to completion.
* Proactively identify improvements to performance or workflows and speak up about them.

**Requirements**

* Existing access to SNF (previously known as RPF at the University of Sydney) and/or UNSW-ANFF.
* Hands-on and/or knowledge of experience in microfabrication processes and tools.
* Strong attention to detail, with a methodical approach to laboratory work and a commitment to maintaining clear and accurate records.
* A fast learner who goes deep – building real understanding, not just surface familiarity.
* Analytical problem solver when the path forward isn’t obvious – breaking problems down and making progress rather than waiting for clarity to arrive.
* Confident enough to contribute ideas around senior team members and grounded enough to learn from them.
* A genuine interest in growing with a fast-paced, innovative company and contributing to the development of transformative technology.

This role would be well suited to students currently studying in Nanotechnology, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Chemistry, Materials Science, or related field.

**Bonus points for:**

* Exposure to semiconductor, MEMS, electrochemistry, PCB, or advanced materials processes.
* Familiarity with metrology tools such as optical microscopy, FIB-SEM, SEM, AFM, or conductivity measurements.

**Why Choose Syenta?**

We’re passionate about building a diverse, people-first company. Our culture of collaboration and mutual respect fuels innovation capable of redefining an industry. At Syenta, you’ll have the opportunity to take ownership, lead high-impact teams, and shape the future of semiconductor manufacturing.

**What We Offer**

* Competitive salary
* Early-stage equity opportunities
* 12% superannuation contributions
* Flexible leave policies and a strong work-life balance
* Professional growth in a high-impact, fast-growing deep-tech startup
* Team events and collaborative culture, including company-wide gatherings in Australia

This is a genuine opportunity to help shape how workforce data, reporting and analytics are delivered across the University and its entities, including Macquarie University Hospital from the ground up.

As our HR Data and Insights Analyst, you'll be the specialist who makes workforce information usable. You'll develop and build dashboards and reports, and translate large, complex datasets into insights and recommendations that University leaders, HR Business Partners and entity leaders rely on for workforce planning, budgeting and day-to-day decisions.

Reporting to the Head, Workforce Planning and Insights, you’ll work at the heart of the university’s people and workforce strategy, collaborating closely with HR Shared Services, HR Applications (IT), Business Intelligence and Reporting, and Finance to deliver meaningful insights and drive informed decision-making.

If you thrive on the full spectrum of people analytics, from data governance and regulatory reporting to generating insights that shape strategic decision-making, this is an exciting opportunity to make a meaningful impact and be part of a dynamic team.

Reporting to the Head, Workforce Planning and Insights, you will:

  

* Partner with University leaders, HR Business Partners, HR Shared Services, Finance, HR Applications (IT) and Business Intelligence and Reporting teams to understand workforce information requirements and deliver effective reporting and analytical solutions.
* Provide specialist workforce planning and analytics expertise through workforce forecasting, scenario modelling and reporting that informs workforce planning, budgeting and decision-making, and contributes to implementation of the University's workforce planning framework.
* Analyse and model workforce establishment, composition, movement and capability data, converting complex information into meaningful reports, actionable insights and recommendations for HR, University and entity leaders.

* Work with HR, HR Applications (IT) and Business Intelligence and Reporting teams to design, build, maintain and continuously improve workforce reports, dashboards and analytical tools that meet stakeholder requirements and deliver accurate, timely and relevant information.
* Keep pace with contemporary developments and emerging practices in workforce analytics, business intelligence and data management, identifying opportunities to strengthen the University's workforce intelligence capability.

**About You**

Bringing together traditional and alternative investments, we provide clients around the world with a dedicated partnership and focus on long-term performance. **PRIVATE EQUITY AND GROWTH EQUITY INVESTING**

The Australia and New Zealand Private Equity and Growth Equity Investing team is involved in various investment opportunities, including buyout private equity, growth equity, value-added infrastructure, and sustainability impact investing.

We form a key part of the firm’s global Private Equity investing group, with access to both a dedicated middle-market buyout and growth capital focused Asia Equity Fund and specialist global equity funds.

Our Private Equity strategy seeks long-term capital appreciation by committing equity to high-quality companies operating in industries with resilient growth, typically in partnership with strong management and founders.

Our Growth strategy seeks to partner with visionary founders and CEOs to build enduring, category-defining businesses by harnessing the global network and deep industry expertise of Goldman Sachs.

job_title: Technical Director PaFX (Houdini) - Netflix Animation Studios
description_text:
Netflix Animation Studios is on a mission to entertain the world with bold, immersive animated films that are timeless and impactful. We are paving the way for the future of animation by building a community of amazing artists and talent across three vibrant locations globally. Come join us!

**Job Summary:**

  

The Procedural Asset and FX Technical Director is a Houdini TD responsible for supporting all teams that use SideFX Houdini. They work with the front-end assets team, such as Surfacing and Modelling, and also back end shot-based teams: FX, Character FX, Crowds, and Matte Painting.
  
  
They assist creative and visual objectives through pipeline troubleshooting, user support, technical direction, and tool development. The TD will participate in the development of artist workflows and tools for projects and debug problematic workflow steps to support global studio productions in that area. The TD will work closely with their craft groups and show leadership, the Solutions Engineering and R&D teams to enable high-quality technical outcomes and a standardized approach.

* Participate in or lead the direction, evolution & maintenance of technology within the PAFX department.
* Design, develop, review and write well-maintainable, production level and consistently high-quality code.
* Track, debug, and resolve workflow issues in partnership with technical supervisors, associate technical supervisors, solutions engineers, and R&D.
* Work closely with other TD’s on the team to drive the technical success of key development initiatives.
* Communicate clearly, via instant messaging systems like Slack, to proactively report on issues that may affect others, provide updates on software releases, and offer assistance to other team members.
* Ensure that technology, tools, and procedures support the creative process.
* Provide solutions to visual problems through existing tools or by leading the implementation of new tools.
* Take responsibility for the troubleshooting & optimization of the tools, software, and workflows of the PAFX department.
* Actively participate in or drive QA, technical testing, and validation of new technology, tool releases, or pipeline changes such that artist workflow is not impacted.
* Understand the processes of adjoining departments and provide input where required to maximize pipeline efficiency and quality.
* Actively participate in brainstorming and problem-solving, contributing technical expertise and insight, to create and maintain technology within the canonical production pipeline.
* Support the organization's overall technical goals as required.
* Demonstrate excellent communication skills, including the ability to clearly present work to stakeholders, actively gather feedback, and incorporate it into technical solutions.
* Be aware of the deadlines for development initiatives and actively engage in keeping these on track.
* Continuously monitor the scope of development initiatives and help to ensure scope adjustments have additional estimates, etc.
* Prioritize and break down technical projects into organized parts and describe them in Jira
* Provide technical guidance to other TDs and TAs, where appropriate, with day-to-day issues and escalation through the right channels when necessary.
* Mentor junior team members and assist in orientation with new starters.
* Create synergies between different work groups to promote efficiency and optimization and to generate innovative ideas and approaches to how we do things
  

  

**What You’ll Need:**

  

Experience:

* 5+ years of proven pipeline TD experience in large-scale animated features, animated TV series, the gaming industry, and/or VFX feature films.
* Solid production/industry experience as a TD, ideally as part of a team.
  

  

Skills/Knowledge:

* Comprehensive Houdini experience with using and troubleshooting procedural node-based workflows.
* A strong understanding of USD and its general concepts, including Houdini’s Solaris/LOP context.
* Proven ability to design and build production-ready Houdini Digital Assets (HDAs) to simplify artist workflows and abstract complex operations.

* Expertise in configuring and customizing the Houdini environment for production use.
* Practical experience in developing custom user interfaces using Python (PySide/PyQt).
* Knowledge of version control software such as git, as well as the ability to code review and troubleshoot problems as they arise in GitHub.
* Knowledge in Python as well as PyQt or another GUI toolkit.
* Knowledge of concepts like data flow, data dependencies, metadata, publishing, and retrieval.
* Knowledge of Flow Production Tracking (Shotgrid).
* Knowledge of software development practices such as Agile and how to apply them in software such as Jira.
* Degree in Animation, Film, Computer Science, Design, Engineering, Math or Physics, or equivalent combination of education & work experience in animation/VFX.
* Knowledge of other DCCs such as Maya, Nuke and/or similar software in the animation domain is a plus.

job_title: Head, Workforce Planning and HR Data Insights
description_text:
The Head of Workforce Planning and Data Insights leads the University's strategic workforce planning, HR reporting and workforce intelligence and insights activities. The role is responsible for establishing and providing a contemporary people analytics capability within the University Group that enables evidence-based insights to support the achievement of the people and organisational culture elements of the University's Strategy and Operational Plan.

As **Head of Workforce Planning and HR Data Insights**, you will create the frameworks, data and insights that help University and entity leaders understand their workforce today and plan for the workforce they will need tomorrow.

Reporting to the Chief People Officer and working as part of the HR Leadership Team, you will guide enterprise workforce planning cycles, scenario modelling and workforce intelligence for the University Group including Macquarie University Hospital. Your work will connect people data to budget planning, operating plans and the people and culture ambitions set out in the University's Strategy and Operational Plan.

This is a genuine opportunity to shape something from the ground up. With a team of two HR Reporting and Insights Analysts, close partnerships across HR, Finance, IT and Business Intelligence, and the chance to apply emerging technologies including AI and advanced analytics, you will help move the conversation from reporting on what happened to anticipating what comes next.

**About the Role**

In this role you will:

  

* Guide enterprise workforce planning cycles and scenario modelling that shape the budget, operating plans and strategic initiatives, and embed the University's workforce planning framework.
* Work alongside the Chief People Officer, HR Leadership Team and HR Business Partners to pinpoint workforce risks, capability gaps and future requirements, turning insight into prioritised action.
* Build and oversee an enterprise-wide people analytics and workforce intelligence function, delivering reporting and evidence-based advice that supports decisions across the Executive Group and the University's entities.
* Set shared HR data governance standards, definitions and reporting frameworks, partnering with HR Shared Services on data quality and accuracy.
* Oversee workforce compliance and external reporting obligations — including the Higher Education Statistics Collection, WGEA, remuneration benchmarking and internal governance reporting — so reporting stays accurate and trusted.
* Partner with Information Technology and Business Intelligence teams to improve workforce systems and reporting tools, and apply emerging technologies such as AI and advanced analytics.
* Guide and develop a team of workforce planning and analytics professionals, bringing people together around collaboration, service excellence, continuous improvement and data literacy.

**About Us**

Macquarie University is a place of inspiration and ideas, where curiosity is encouraged and where people are given the scope to make a real contribution. Human Resources provides advice and services to the University and its controlled entities across attraction, selection, performance, development and remuneration, and oversees leadership capability and workforce compliance.

  

The Workforce Planning and Data Insights team is one of four specialist teams alongside Talent Acquisition, Capability, Culture and Inclusion, and Employee Relations that partner with the Chief People Officer, HR Business Partners and University leaders.

**About You**

You are an experienced workforce planning or people analytics professional who enjoys turning complex data into clear direction. You are comfortable in the detail of datasets and equally comfortable in the room with executives, and you bring the credibility, curiosity and judgement needed to establish a new capability in a large, multi-entity organisation.

**Selection Criteria**

  

* Extensive experience in workforce planning, people analytics and/or HR reporting in a large, complex organisation.
* Proven record of scenario modelling and workforce forecasting that informs budget and operating plans.
* Demonstrated skill in translating workforce data into clear insights and recommendations for executive audiences.
* Experience establishing data governance standards, definitions and reporting frameworks, with a focus on data quality.
* Working knowledge of workforce compliance and reporting obligations (for example WGEA, sector statistical collections, remuneration benchmarking).
* Experience with HRIS, business intelligence and analytics tools, and interest in applying emerging technologies such as AI.
* Experience guiding and developing a team, with a collaborative, service-focused approach to partnering across an organisation.

**About the Department**
------------------------

The Department of Industry, Science and Resources and our broader portfolio are integral to the Australian Government’s economic agenda. Our purpose is to help the government build a better future for all Australians through enabling a productive, resilient and sustainable economy, enriched by science and technology. We do this by:

* Growing innovative & competitive businesses, industries and regions
* Investing in science and technology
* Strengthening the resources sector.

The APS and the department offer a clear direction and meaningful work. You will be able to create positive impact in people’s lives whilst contributing to improved outcomes for Australia and our people.  
  
If you would like to feel a strong connection to your work and you are accountable, committed and open to change, join us in shaping Australia’s future.  
  
Please see the APSC’s APS Employee Value Proposition for more information on the benefits and value of employment within the APS.  

**About the team**
------------------

**The National Measurement Institute**  
  
We are the Australian Government’s national authority on measurement.  
  
At the National Measurement Institute (NMI), we empower innovation and protect trust in Australian industry and society through world-class measurement science. Join a team where your expertise drives national impact, your curiosity is nurtured, and the work you do creates trusted measurement for a fair, safe, healthy, and competitive Australia. Our employees enjoy career development opportunities, flexible working arrangements and the opportunity to shape Australia’s economic future through world-class measurement science.  
  
At NMI, precision meets purpose.  
  
We’re committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and impactful workplace by hiring people who share our values and bring integrity, collaboration, and innovation to everything they do.  
  
**Physical Metrology Branch**  
  
NMI’s Physical Metrology Branch provides Australia’s peak measurement standards for physical quantities. This enables measurements made in Australia to be accepted internationally, which is particularly important for trade. Our people share their expertise by providing measurement services from calibration and testing to technical advice and training. We contribute actively to international measurement forums and enhance our capabilities through research and development in line with national and international requirements.  
  
**Power Systems Technology Team**  
  
NMI's Power Systems Technology team develops advanced measurement technologies and delivers specialist testing and calibration services that support Australia's electricity network and clean energy transition. The team operates Australia's largest high-voltage and high-current laboratory and provides critical services to electric power utilities, equipment manufacturers and industry stakeholders. Supporting Australia's Net Zero ambitions, our work underpins the generation, storage, transmission and use of clean energy. Its capabilities span three key areas: high-voltage testing and calibration, calibration of power system voltage and current sensors, and the design and manufacture of highly accurate digital and analogue measurement systems.  
  
The team delivers more than 30 specialised testing and calibration services across a diverse range of power system equipment and measurement parameters. It also undertakes applied research in collaboration with universities, national metrology institutes and industry partners to develop innovative measurement techniques and technologies. Our team's experts contribute to the development of Australian and international standards through active participation in Standards Australia and the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC). We provide technical leadership across a range of national and international working groups, helping shape the future of power system measurement science and engineering.

**The opportunity**
-------------------

This is a senior opportunity for an experienced electrical or power system engineer to apply their expertise to nationally significant infrastructure and measurement challenges. The role supports Australia’s high-voltage and high-current measurement capability, helping ensure that critical electricity infrastructure can be tested, calibrated and assessed with confidence.  
  
The Senior Electrical Scientist/Metrologist will work at the interface of practical power engineering, specialised measurement systems and national standards. The role involves leading or contributing to high-value testing and calibration services, capability development, applied research, stakeholder engagement, and representation in national and international technical forums.  
  
As the electricity sector evolves—with increasing renewable generation, high-voltage transmission, power electronics, grid-scale storage and emerging electrical infrastructure—the role offers the opportunity to shape measurement capability that is directly relevant to industry, regulators and the national electricity system.

**What’s in it for you?**
-------------------------

Join a community of professionals committed to technical measurement excellence and cutting-edge research. We invest in advanced facilities, foster collaboration with leading institutions, and support innovation in areas that include nanometrology, sports integrity, forensic analysis, cancer diagnostics, high voltage electricity, and clean energy. You will work with people who have diverse skill sets including scientists, engineers, policy specialists and regulatory professionals.  
  
You will build sought-after experience leading nationally significant high-voltage testing, calibration and capability development, while deepening your expertise in measurement science and national standards.  
  
As part of the Department of Industry, Science and Resources, employees at NMI are covered by an enterprise agreement and benefits include:

* Parental leave
* a vacation care subsidy
* $235 annual healthy lifestyle subsidy
* access to study assistance
* access to Employee Assistance Program - health, wellbeing, counselling and support when needed.

For candidates with highly specialised skills and experience, remuneration above the standard salary may be considered through an Individual Flexibility Arrangement (IFA), subject to delegate approval and departmental policy.

**Our ideal candidate**
-----------------------

* Leadership skills in a technical or scientific environment.
* Experience developing, operating or maintaining complex measurement, testing or calibration systems involving high-voltage and high-current applications.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving and innovation skills, including the ability to develop new measurement capabilities and improve existing test and calibration services.
* Demonstrated ability to build productive relationships with clients, regulators, standards bodies, industry stakeholders and scientific peers.
* Strong communication skills, including the ability to present technical information to a range of audiences and contribute to scientific publications, technical committees and professional forums.
* Demonstrated commitment to safe work practices, quality assurance and continuous improvement.

Additional qualities sought at the S&T8 level include:  

* Demonstrated leadership of scientific or technical teams, including mentoring and capability building.
* Experience developing strategic capability roadmaps, investment priorities and long-term technical programs.
* Demonstrated leadership and influence in technical forums related to national and international standards, accreditation or research.
* Recognition as a technical authority within a specialised field of measurement science or engineering.

**Qualifications**  

* Tertiary qualifications in Electrical Engineering, Physics or a closely related discipline.
* A postgraduate qualification or PhD in a relevant field would be highly regarded but is not essential.

*We’re looking for individuals who bring personal integrity and a sense of purpose, and who embody NMI values (Inclusive, Innovative, Accountable, Adaptable, Influential, and Strategic) while upholding the APS Code of Conduct. Our department has a commitment to inclusion and diversity, with an ambition of being the best possible place to work. This reflects the importance we place on our people and on creating a workplace culture where each and every one of us is valued and respected for our contribution. Our ideal candidate adds to this culture and our workplace in their own way. Even if you’re not sure you meet all the requirements, we’d love to hear from you!*

**What you will do**
--------------------

* Lead or contribute to the development, maintenance and improvement of Australia's national high-voltage and high-current measurement standards, reference systems, traceability chains, uncertainty analyses and specialist capabilities.
* Deliver and oversee complex testing, calibration and measurement services, applying expert technical knowledge to solve complex measurement challenges and provide authoritative advice to clients and stakeholders.
* Drive innovation, research and service development activities to address emerging measurement needs and support future capability requirements within Australia's electricity sector.
* Lead or contribute to strategic capability, workforce and infrastructure planning, while providing technical leadership, supervision and mentoring to scientific and technical staff.
* Ensure laboratory operations comply with ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation requirements, NMI quality systems, technical procedures and workplace health and safety obligations.
* Build and maintain productive stakeholder relationships and represent NMI and Australia in national and international technical committees, standards development activities, accreditation forums, conferences and industry events.

**Classification Expectations**  
  
*S&T7*  
  
At the S&T7 level, the successful candidate will typically:  

* Lead complex technical projects with the potential and willingness to develop into a leading national authority in power systems testing and calibration.
* Provide specialist technical advice within their field of expertise.
* Supervise and develop staff, including mentoring early-career scientists.
* Contribute to strategic planning and future capability development.
* Build effective relationships with stakeholders and clients to achieve program outcomes.

*S&T8*  
  
At the S&T8 level, the successful candidate will in addition:  

* Provide strategic leadership for Australia's high-voltage and high-current measurement capability.
* Lead a team and allocate resources to achieve organisational objectives and national priorities.
* Influence technical directions, measurement strategies and standards development at a national and international level.
* Develop and implement long-term capability roadmaps and investment priorities.
* Act as a recognised national authority on power systems testing and calibration.
* Represent NMI in senior national and international forums and partnerships.

**Eligibility**
---------------

To be eligible for employment in the APS and the department, candidates must be Australian Citizens.  
  
Positions require a Baseline security clearance and successful candidates will be required to obtain and maintain a clearance at this level.

**Notes**
---------

A merit pool may be established and used to fill future vacancies within 18 months from the date the vacancy was first advertised in the Gazette.  
  
The department does currently offer flexible work opportunities for many roles. This position is based at NMI’s Lindfield headquarters in New South Wales, although flexible or remote work arrangements may be considered. Please reach out to the contact officer to discuss this further.

**Application information**
---------------------------

Your application must not contain any classified or sensitive information. This includes in your application responses, CV and any other documents. The selection panel may not consider applications containing classified information.  
  
Please provide a pitch explaining how your skills, knowledge and experience will be relevant to this role and why you are the best candidate for the position. Your pitch can contain no more than 1000 words and should align to the key duties listed above.  
  
You may use AI tools to support your application. However, all content must be accurate, authentic, and reflect your own capability in line with APS merit principles. For further guidance, please refer to the APSC’s Principles for candidate use of AI in recruitment.

Accessible application documentation is available in other formats on request. Please contact recruitment@industry.gov.au or (02) 6276 1235 if you require assistance with your application.  
  
Please refer to our Applying for a position information for additional information on how to apply.

**ABOUT ASI**

ASI (Adam Smith International) is a global advisory company that works locally to transform lives by making economies stronger, societies safer, and governments more effective. We work on behalf of governments, foundations and companies that share our ambition to take on the big challenges facing the world. We develop strategies and design, deliver and evaluate programmes that stimulate economic growth, stability and good governance.

For nearly three decades in almost 100 countries, we have been working in partnership with governments, the private sector and civil society in countries at all stages of development. Our core team of staff and technical experts, in multiple offices around the world, ensures the quality of delivery and high ethical standards that we and our clients require. We bring together a global network of specialist experts, who contribute their experience and know-how, where and when it is needed.

ASI (Australia) Pty Ltd is a wholly owned subsidiary of Adam Smith International. It was established in February 2012 as the company’s Asia Pacific regional office, responsible for leading business development and project delivery across the region. Headquartered in Sydney, the company’s Asia Pacific office is responsible for the management of our portfolio of projects funded by the Australian Aid Programe (managed by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade) and other donors. Managers perform a key role in ASI’s consulting model and play a central part in managing the technical, financial and operational performance of projects. The Assistant Manager will perform project administration activities, supporting and learning from experienced Managers in the team. This is an exciting time to join Adam Smith International and become part of a team of bright, dynamic and committed people, determined to transform lives for the better.

* Tracking and providing expenditure documentation to support client billing

Efficient and effective project management support

* Hold an undergraduate degree in a relevant subject across either the development sector (e.g. development, international relations, political studies) or management (e.g. business administration, program management, organisational development)
